items.title: Healing music ritual
items.names: Shach Chukbar, laying: Khoza Ampar, and Alexa Ampar
items.originalNames: Чукбар Шач, Ампар Хоза (Гуаза), Ампар Алыкса
items.notes: The image shows Abkhazian folk singer and storyteller Shach Chukbar playing an apkhartsa (a two-stringed bowed instrument) at the bedside of the ailing Khoza Ampar in Abkhazia, around 1929. Performances like this were used to comfort the sick, promote healing, and soothe spirits.
items.draft: A photograph dating approximately to 1927 - 1929 from Kaldakhvara, Abkhazia, featuring folk singer and storyteller Shach Chukbar (left) playing the apkhartsa, a two-stringed bowed instrument, at the bedside of the sick Khoza Ampar, with Alexa Ampar on the right. Such performances were meant to comfort the sick and help them heal.
checks: Positions taken from the Russian caption on the photo: "Слева на право: Чукбар Шач, Ампар Гуаза, Ампар Алыкса" (left to right). The caption spells the names Guaza and Alyksa; the names field has Khoza and Alexa. Which spelling?
Date taken is a range (1927 - 1929) and the notes say "around 1929". Draft says "approximately 1927 - 1929".

items.title: Chapshe
items.names: Lying down is Talib Khataovich Kubov, Seated on a chair at the head of the bed on the left is the bonesetter Makhmud Azashikov; standing on the right is the "Dae" Khadjikhan Shalikhovna
items.keywords: Azze the healer, "Dae" a young woman who cares for the patient until recovery, plowshare and a hammer, neckless
items.notes: One of the rituals when a person gets sick is that people visit and play music, sing, and play games in merrying atmosphere, believing hat helps the ill to recover quickly and show the respect and hostality to the mighty (lord) of sickness and health (Sozeresh). Residents of the Circassian village of Khakurinokhabl perform a traditional healing ritual, "Klapshch," in connection with a broken leg sustained by 15-year-old rider Talib Kubov during a race. Seated on a chair at the head of the bed on the left is the bonesetter Makhmud Azashikov; standing on the right is the "Dae"—a young woman who cares for the patient until recovery—Khadjikhan Shalikhovna Meretukova. On the ground in front of the patient's bed lie a plowshare and a hammer; every visitor was required to strike the plowshare with the hammer upon arrival.
items.draft: A 1927 photograph by V. Kanatov from Hakurynehebl, Adygea, showing villagers performing the healing ritual Chapshe for Talib Kubov, a 15-year-old rider who broke his leg in a race. Beside his bed are the bonesetter Makhmud Azashikov (seated, left) and the "Dae" Khadjikhan Meretukova (standing, right), the young woman who nursed him.
checks: Ritual name: title Chapshe, notes "Klapshch", original КӀапщэ. Which to use?
